title: Choose an Analytics metric
lead: Choose a Dashboard metric that answers your question, then check its unit, aggregation and playback population. When building a custom query, retain the corresponding API field names and conditions.

blocks.text: Use Audience for viewing activity, Quality of Experience for startup and buffering, and Top Errors for playback failures. Keep the Analytics license, period and filters consistent. Read quality values together with their corresponding playback counts or viewing duration.

These metrics describe audience and playback quality. The table also gives API aggregation examples. Available Dashboard fields depend on the view; use the API for custom groupings or aggregates, and check collector support.

rows: Sessions that displayed a first frame. The positive-startup filter distinguishes this from the app's unfiltered impression button.
Milliseconds. The Observability catalog also supports average and percentile; its default is median.
Milliseconds in the played state. Divide by 3,600,000 for hours.
Percent of time spent waiting for media during viewing. This is distinct from average BUFFERED duration.
Bits/second (bps). Divide by 1,000,000 for Mbps. This is rendition bitrate, not network throughput.
Measured segment-download speed in bits/second. Field availability depends on the collector.
Percentage against sessions considered, including cases that can fail before video starts. Keep its denominator when comparing results.
Milliseconds for a seek to resume playback.

blocks.text: The official dashboard reference lists download bandwidth and downloaded-data limitations on AVFoundation and Bitmovin iOS. An absent field or empty result on one SDK is not a zero measurement, and does not establish support on every platform.

items: count answers how many; sum answers the total; avg answers the arithmetic mean. The metric defines what is counted or averaged.
median is the 50th percentile. A high percentile, such as p95, describes the slow tail rather than the typical viewer. A percentile query needs its percentile parameter and a supported metric.
The local Web panel uses fixed queries. It does not offer median, percentile, arbitrary periods or free-form filters. Its proxy supports only a subset of the Query API.
Do not average percentages from unequal populations or add unique-user counts across buckets and assume a period total. Keep the metric definition and population visible.

blocks.text: If you use the local aggregate panel

In local development, open Bitmovin Analytics (server-proxied query). Every button queries the server-selected Analytics license over the last 7 days, without time buckets or category filters. The displayed numbers keep their API units.

rows: Impression/session count; not automatically the dashboard Plays metric.
Intent to play to the first frame; milliseconds (ms).
Average buffering duration; milliseconds (ms), not a percentage.

blocks.text: The browser-local startup readout measures SourceLoaded to Playing. Analytics VIDEO_STARTUPTIME measures playback initiation to the first frame, while STARTUPTIME also includes player setup. Equal units do not make these measurements interchangeable.
Keep names, units and populations together

Use uppercase REST attributes such as VIDEO_STARTUPTIME exactly as documented. Observability MCP uses its own catalog keywords, such as video_startuptime and plays, and can add metric-specific filters. Resolve those keywords with searchMetrics when available, or getAvailableMetrics, rather than assuming that a dashboard label is an API field.

The MCP catalog distinguishes error_percentage from error_ratio, which is normalized by viewing hours. Neither is the browser's Error event count. Before deriving a new rate, verify the selected metric's definition, unit and denominator in the dashboard/API catalog.
